description: Whether two topic labels name the same subject. Merging is the decision that cannot be reviewed by reading the prompt: too strict and one subject spreads across rows that never reach the promotion threshold, too loose and every specific question in a domain collapses into one useless bucket. These are the pairs that mark the boundary. Every example here is invented — none of it comes from a real workspace, and none of it should.

cases.name: rephrasing
cases.why: "store shift scheduling" vs "staff rota planning": the two phrasings mean the same thing in different words. They share almost no characters, so only the model tier can decide.

cases.name: elaboration
cases.why: "chain store shift scheduling" vs "store shift scheduling": one has one qualifier fewer and still names the same thing.

cases.name: harmless qualifier
cases.why: "order API rate limiting" vs "order API rate limiting issues": the word "issues" does not change the subject.

cases.name: abbreviation
cases.why: "CI pipeline" vs "continuous integration pipeline": an abbreviation and its full name are the same thing, yet share almost no characters.

cases.name: specific lookup inside a broad subject
cases.incoming: 三号仓库上月入库单号
cases.why: "warehouse inbound process" vs "warehouse No. 3 last month's inbound receipt numbers": same area, but this is a one-off specific query, not the same standing interest. Folding it in turns the interest into a bucket that holds everything.

cases.name: different question in the same domain
cases.why: "order API rate limiting" vs "order API authentication": two different things about the same API.

cases.name: hyponym
cases.why: "backend architecture choices" vs "order API rate limit tuning": a narrower concept is not the same thing, or a broad topic would absorb the whole domain.

cases.name: two aspects of one thing
cases.why: "annual audit material preparation" vs "annual audit inquiry replies": two stages of one thing that care about different things. Merges like this really happened in production.

cases.name: broad subject versus a lookup in it
cases.why: "annual party organization" vs "annual party sign-up lookup": organizing an event and checking who signed up are different things. Merges like this really happened in production.

cases.name: unrelated
cases.why: "store shift scheduling" vs "order API rate limiting": unrelated, and no tier should merge them.

cases.name: same word different field
cases.why: "image segmentation model tuning" vs "database sharding": sharing one character (meaning "divide") makes no relationship.

granularity.note: A topic must be a recurring area, not a single question. A label that carries a person's name, a number, a date, a version or a quantity can only ever match itself: it is counted once, stays at 1 forever, and the threshold means nothing. The questions are about warehouse No. 3's inbound receipts last month, the orders API page-size default in v2.3, and how to reach the settlement platform's business contact.

cases.question: 三号仓库上个月的入库单号有哪些？
cases.bad: 三号仓库2026年3月入库单号查询记录

cases.question: v2.3 版本 orders 接口的分页参数默认值是多少？
cases.bad: v2.3版本orders接口分页参数默认值查询
